The *Navattabbaṁsaṁghassadinnaṁmahapphalantikathā* ("Debate on the proposition that it should not be said that what is given to the Saṅgha brings great fruit") is a debate within the seventeenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Theravāda *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of a thematic cluster in the seventeenth chapter concerning gifts and the Saṅgha, closely related in formulaic structure and content to neighboring debates such as Kv 17.6 (*Navattabbaṁsaṁghodakkhiṇaṁpaṭiggaṇhātikathā*), Kv 17.7 (*Navattabbaṁsaṁghodakkhiṇaṁvisodhetītikathā*), and Kv 17.10 (*Navattabbaṁbuddhassadinnaṁmahapphalantikathā*) [DharmaNexus].
SuttaCentral notes curated passage-level parallels to two poetic texts from the *Khuddakanikāya*: the *Daddallavimānavatthu* (Vv 34) and the *Vihāravimānavatthu* (Vv 44) [SuttaCentral]. The core theme of giving to the Saṅgha and its fruits is also cited in connection with the *Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 142), the *Gotamivatthadānapañha* of the *Milindapañha* (Mil 6.1.2), the *Yajamānasutta* (SN 11.16), and several canonical and commentarial texts preserved in Chinese (including MĀ 180, T 84, T 202.52, T 203.50, T 212.14, T 1509.22, and T 1545.178) and Tibetan (Up 4.103) [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse computations from DharmaNexus confirm substantial shared material within the Pali corpus. Specifically, Kv 17.9 shares extended passages with Vv 34 (§§5.1–10.4) and Vv 44 (§§5.4–10.4), agreeing with SuttaCentral's curated parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Extensive text reuse is also recorded with the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, Mil 6.1.2, SN 11, and various suttas in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3, AN 4, AN 7, and AN 8) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further identifies cross-language segment alignments with the alternative Chinese translation of the *Saṃyuktāgama* (別譯雜阿含經, T 100) and Tibetan canonical texts [DharmaNexus].
